say: When a storm could push the sea three metres higher, Rotterdam shuts its river with two floating doors.
Each one is two hundred and ten metres long.
Most days, they hide in dry docks.
When a surge is coming, the docks flood and the hollow doors float.
Motors swing them out on ball joints ten metres wide.
In the middle, they fill with water and sink to the riverbed.
Now a steel wall holds back the North Sea.
When the storm passes, they're pumped empty and float home.
Follow for how the world is really engineered.
